name: How do tenant improvement allowances work for office build-outs in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Who pays for what in an office build-out when the lease includes a tenant improvement allowance?
mainEntity.text: Who pays for what in an office build-out when the lease includes a tenant improvement allowance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tenant improvement allowances are a major factor in office build-outs because they can reduce upfront cash needs, but they rarely cover everything. The allowance is typically negotiated in the lease and may be paid as reimbursement after work is completed or built into rent economics. What it covers depends on the deal, the building class, the lease term, and the tenant’s credit profile. In many Los Angeles-area projects, the allowance may cover standard interior improvements, while the tenant funds premium finishes, extra conference rooms, custom millwork, specialized HVAC, or technology-heavy requirements. Before signing, tenants should verify whether the allowance includes design, permits, sales tax, management fees, and contingency. They should also confirm payment timing, because reimbursement after completion affects cash flow. A clean scope and allowance breakdown helps avoid surprises during construction.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tenant improvement allowance is money the landlord contributes toward office improvements, usually negotiated in the lease. It may cover part of the construction, but tenants often still pay for upgrades beyond the allowance, design fees, permits, furniture, and any scope added after the lease is signed.
